## What Does the Cook Hearing Delay Mean for the Fed?


Cook keeps her seat on the Fed board for now: the White House "committee of inquiry" moved her hearing from Thursday to Dec. 14, according to[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/04/trump-federal-reserve-lisa-cook-hearing.html) , and the Supreme Court's June ruling left in place a lower court order blocking her termination while her lawsuit proceeds. A White House official said Cook requested the postponement.


Per CNBC, Trump set up the committee in early October to investigate allegations that Cook made false statements related to "one or more mortgage instruments" and to report whether there is "cause" for her removal. Cook denies any wrongdoing, and her lawyer, Abbe Lowell, has said she "will be executing her official duties as Governor at financial and monetary policy meetings in Europe."


According to the Federal Reserve's[FOMC statement](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261028a.htm) of Oct. 28, the committee held the federal funds target range at 3-3/4 to 4 percent by a 10-2 vote, with Cook and Beth Hammack dissenting in favor of a quarter-point hike.


## When Is the Next FOMC Meeting?


The next FOMC meeting is Dec. 8-9, according to the Federal Reserve's[meeting calendar](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm) , ahead of Cook's rescheduled Dec. 14 hearing.[Kitco](https://www.kitco.com/news/article/2026-11-04/gold-and-silver-surge-democratic-midterm-sweep-drives-dollar-yields-lower) reported that markets put the chance of a rate hike at that meeting near 80%.
